summary: Tom Ginsburg is a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999). He held positions at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) and the University of Chicago (~2008).

Tom Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May (~1978–1989). He served as Emeritus Professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary (~2016).
Tomohiro Manabe is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held an attested post as lecturer at Waseda University in 2020 and as Associate Professor at Hokkaido University in 2026.
Tomoko Makidono is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She was a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa, working in religious studies and history/archaeology, studied at International Christian University, Yale University, and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 1985). She held faculty posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and University of Michigan (1999, ~2001–2021).
Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as full-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012) and professor at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012) and served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He also served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a special researcher at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Madras under C. S. Sundaram and Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal (PhD). He held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Canterbury under Jim Wilson, Paul Harrison, and William Sax (PhD 1993), later holding professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2009).

Tony K. Stewart is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011–2021).

Torakazu Doi was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe (~1923–1926). He held academic posts at Sagami Women's University (~1952–1964) and Dokkyo University (~1964–1971).

Torkel Brekke works in religious studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo and Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later holding posts at Oslo, PRIO (2016–2020), Oslo Metropolitan University (2019–2023), and MF Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society (2023).

Toru Funayama is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991–1992). He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology who studied at Tokyo and Kyoto universities. He held multiple posts at Kyoto University (1909–1948), the Toho Gakkai (1947), and the Institute of Eastern Culture (~1947–1955).

Toru Kumeji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He has held positions at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as a senior researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).

Toru Sagara was a scholar in philosophy and Japanology who studied under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held posts at Ibaraki University (~1950–1963), the University of Tokyo (~1963–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1992).

Toru Takahashi was a Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1898–1902). He held posts including professor at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, he held posts at Lausanne (attested 1998–2000), IKGA (attested 2006), the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015), and COHD (attested 2016–2018).
